# How the FM-1 MIDI dongle was designed: tooling and rules

A record of the tools, pipeline, rules and checks Claude used to take this board from a spec to a routed,
fab-ready KiCad project. It is written as raw material for a reusable skill. Everything below is what was
actually run on this machine (KiCad 10.0.6, Python 3.14, Arch/Omarchy) between 2026-10-17 and 2026-10-20.

---

## 1. The core idea: the board is generated by code, not edited by hand

Every design artifact is the output of a script in `tools/`. Changing the design means editing a script and
re-running the pipeline, never clicking in KiCad. This gives:

- **Reproducibility:** the whole board rebuilds from scratch in seconds.
- **Reviewable diffs:** a placement or a route is one line of Python (`'U5': (6.82, 5.5, 90)`).
- **Numeric checks:** every rule can be checked in code, because the board is data.
- **Works for someone who can't open KiCad:** every stage ends in PNG renders.

```
DESIGN.md (locked spec)
   │
   ▼
tools/gen_sch.py      → .kicad_sch, .kicad_pro, project .kicad_sym      gate: ERC 0
   │
   ▼
tools/gen_pcb.py      → .kicad_pcb (outline, placement, planes)           gate: 0 placement issues
   │
   ▼
apply_rules.py        → .kicad_pro net classes + .kicad_dru               (pcb-house-rules skill)
   │
   ▼
tools/route.py        → tracks, vias, pours, zone fill                     gate: DRC 0 unconnected
   │
   ▼
tools/silk.py         → silkscreen regenerated                             gate: all designators placed
   │
   ▼
checks: kicad-cli DRC, check_routing.py, tools/check_loops.py
renders: render_route.py, render_nets.py, kicad-cli svg + 3D
cost: jlc_bom.py        release (only when asked): fab_release.py
```

**Ordering gotcha:** `gen_sch.py` rewrites `.kicad_pro`, so `apply_rules.py` must run after it, or the net
classes are lost.

---

## 2. Tools

### 2.1 Base software

| Tool | Used for |
|---|---|
| KiCad 10 `pcbnew` Python module | Placement, routing, zones, silk: every board edit |
| `kicad-cli sch erc` | Schematic electrical rules check |
| `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --format json` | Design rules check, parsed as JSON |
| `kicad-cli pcb export svg` + `rsvg-convert` | Per-layer 2D images (`docs/route_*.png`, `silk_*.png`) |
| `kicad-cli pcb render --quality high --rotate X,Y,Z` | 3D renders (`docs/views/*`, `docs/pcb3d_*`) |
| `pdftotext` | Reading datasheets (pinouts, logic tables) |
| matplotlib | Custom review renders (ratsnest, routed copper) |
| WebSearch / WebFetch | Datasheets, LCSC/JLC pages, prices, competitors |

### 2.2 Project scripts (`tools/`)

| Script | Lines | Job |
|---|---|---|
| `gen_sch.py` | ~400 | Writes the schematic as an s-expression. Symbols are copied from `/usr/share/kicad/symbols` into `lib_symbols`, so the file is self-contained. Missing symbols (SY6280, SN74LVC1G3157) are drawn in code and also written to `fm1_dongle.kicad_sym`. Every connection is a net label on a short stub, so the netlist is correct by construction. |
| `gen_pcb.py` | ~400 | Outline (rounded corners, case notches), the `PLACE` table `{ref: (x, y, rot)}`, layer stackup, GND/3V3 planes. Ends with numeric checks: pad spacing, pads under bodies, courtyard overlap, pads at edge, holes. Auto-flips 2-pin passives so the pads face their nets. |
| `route.py` | ~200 | Hand routing in code. Each track is an explicit polyline: `path(net, layer, width, *points)` and `via(net, x, y, size)`. Then pours and zone fill. |
| `silk.py` | ~360 | Removes all library silk (from the file text, see gotchas) and redraws: body outlines clipped away from pads and the edge, pin-1 dots, LED cathode marks, every designator placed by search with fallbacks, back-side labels. |
| `check_loops.py` | ~60 | Union-find over tracks, vias and pads per net: cycles = edges − nodes + groups. Must be 0. Also reports the longest 45° segment per net. |
| `render_nets.py` | ~110 | Placement plus ratsnest (minimum spanning tree per net), pads coloured by net. |
| `render_route.py` | ~110 | F.Cu and B.Cu side by side at real track widths, pours shaded by net. |
| `export_jlc.sh` | small | BOM export from the schematic in JLC columns. |

### 2.3 Claude Code skills (`~/.claude/skills`)

| Skill | Used for |
|---|---|
| `hardware-design-flow` | The map: schematic → parts/cost → rules → floorplan → route → review → release → order |
| `pcb-house-rules` | `apply_rules.py` (net classes and `.kicad_dru` from `house_rules.yaml`), `check_routing.py` (style audit: angles, 90° corners, acid traps, long 45° runs), `impedance_calc.py` |
| `pcb-floorplan` | Placement method and checks (brief → plan → place → check loop) |
| `jlc-bom-cost` | `jlc_bom.py --boards N --mode standard`: prices every BOM line at the real quantity, plus Extended fees. Uses an offline JLC part DB with live re-pricing. |
| `jlc-fab-release` | `fab_release.py`: Gerbers, BOM and CPL with rotation fixes, gated on DRC/ERC. Intended errors are accepted per item only with the owner's sign-off. |
| `kicad`, `emc`, `datasheets`, `lcsc`, `bom`, `jlcpcb` | Kicad-happy set: schematic/PCB analysis, datasheet extraction, LCSC lookup |
| `kicad-pcb-autorouter-workflow`, `pcb-autoroute` | Installed. **Not used** after the owner rejected autorouting (see 3.1). |

### 2.4 Footprints and 3D models

- **EasyEDA/LCSC footprints** go in `fm1_dongle.pretty` for every part JLC will place, so pads match JLC's own
  library exactly (QFN-28, PJ-320D, USB-C plug and socket, SOT-23s, SOP-6).
- **KiCad stock footprints** are used for 0603 passives, SOD-123 and SC-70-6.
- **STEP models are vendored** into `fm1_dongle.3dshapes` (KiCad's 3D library isn't installed here). They come
  from gitlab kicad-packages3D (CC-BY-SA) or the EasyEDA export. Every connector must show in the 3D render.

## 3. Rules

### 3.1 Owner rules (process)

These came from the owner's corrections and outrank everything else.

1. **Stop at the stage that was asked for.** A floorplan request means placement, planes and keep-outs only.
   Never autoroute, never produce fab outputs unless asked. Offer, don't do. (The owner was angry about an
   unasked autoroute.)
2. **Never autoroute.** Routing is the owner's craft. When routing was requested it was done as explicit
   hand-chosen polylines in `route.py`, never by a router.
3. **Verify every hardware fact before stating it:** part numbers, LCSC tier (Basic/Extended), price, stock,
   pinout, chip features. Fetch the datasheet or LCSC/JLC page and cite it. Anything unchecked is labelled
   "unverified". (Past mistakes: wrong tiers, and an MCU variant that had no USB host.)
4. **Always deliver images.** The owner reviews renders, not KiCad files. Render and look at the images
   yourself before reporting.
5. **Commit or push only when asked.** Work on a branch (`pcb-v4-routed`), not main.
6. **The owner signs off on accepted DRC errors**, never Claude (`--accept-current`).
7. **No bulky parts.** No pin headers: programming is 3 bare test pads. Prefer small packages.
8. **If a skill is missing, find one online and install it.**

### 3.1b Schematic drawing rules (owner, 2026-10-20)

- Power and ground connect through KiCad `power:` symbols (global power ports: GND, +3V3, +5V, VBUS, or a custom
  power symbol for a board rail), never plain net-label text. Signal nets may use labels.
- No symbol, reference, value, pin label or net label may overlap another. Lay out by functional block with spacing,
  then render the sheet (`kicad-cli sch export svg`) and check overlaps numerically and visually.
- v4 failed both: it used text labels for +3V3/GND/+5V_IN/VBUS_FM1, and U2, U3, U4, U5, J1, J3/J4 and D2 overlapped.

### 3.2 Layout rules (owner + IPC-2221/2222 practice)

**Placement by priority:**
1. USB differential pair first: MCU pins facing the connector, straight, same layer, no vias, unbroken GND
   plane under it.
2. Power next: entry → load switch → LDO → loads, placed on the side the MCU's power pins face.
3. Serial/low-speed (MIDI, SWD) last, on the side those pins face.

**Orientation:** every part, including 0603 passives, is turned so its pads face the nets they connect to.
No part where the trace has to wrap around its own body.

**GND return:** In1 = solid GND plane, In2 = 3V3 plane, GND pours on F.Cu and B.Cu. Few vias.

**Mechanics:**
- Connector mating direction and mating clearances.
- Two moulded TRS plugs side by side need a 10 mm jack pitch.
- Nothing in the USB plug's clamp zone (1.5 mm).
- Captured case: side notches, no screw holes.

**Single-sided assembly** whenever possible (cheaper JLC PCBA).

**Numeric collision checks.** Don't trust EasyEDA courtyards: they are body-only. Check pad-to-pad, pad-to-body,
courtyard and edge distances in code. Skip pad pairs on the same net.

### 3.3 Routing rules (Electronic Cats house rules + owner)

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Vias | 0.6/0.3 for signal and GND stitching, 0.8/0.4 for power. No other sizes. |
| Tracks | 0.2 signal, 0.3 power next to fine-pitch pads, 0.5 power |
| Clearance / copper-to-edge / hole-to-hole | 0.2 / 0.5 / 0.25 mm |
| Angles | Orthogonal runs. Every bend is a short 45° transition. No 90° corners, no acute angles, no any-angle segments, no long 45° runs. |
| Topology | Every signal net is a tree: 0 loops. Power nets are trees of tracks plus pours. |
| Planes | GND plane under all signals, power by pours or planes |
| Thermals | Small pads on the GND pour get a solid connection (`ZONE_CONNECTION_FULL`) where thermal spokes would be starved |
| USB full-speed on a thin board | Plain 0.2 mm, no impedance target. 12 Mbps over a 2.6 mm run doesn't need 90 Ω, and JLC has no 0.8 mm impedance stackup. Recorded in the project `house_rules.yaml`. |

### 3.4 Silkscreen rules

- One consistent style. Library silk is removed.
- Lines ≥ 0.15 mm; ≥ 0.2 mm from mask openings; ≥ 0.3 mm inside the board edge.
- Designators are 0.8 mm (owner's choice, below JLC's 1.0 mm). Each sits next to its part, clear of pads,
  bodies, edges and other text. Fallback: inside the part's own outline when it is big enough.
- Pin-1 dot on every IC (fallback: a 0.3 mm dot), cathode mark on diodes and LEDs.
- Test pads are labelled with their signal (3V3/DIO/GND), not their designator.
- Back side: board name, revision, jack names.
- Parts JLC places are left as they are; a designator that doesn't fit stays on F.Fab and is reported.

### 3.5 Parts and cost rules (JLCPCB)

- Every part has an `LCSC#` field (Electronic Cats convention) and `manf#`.
- Prefer Basic and Preferred-Extended parts. Each unique Extended part adds a feeder fee.
- Price at the real order quantity, plus attrition (`--boards N`).
- BOM.csv has a verification note per line: what was checked, where and when.
- Standard vs Economic PCBA follows the parts: J1 is soldered on both faces, so this board is Standard.

---

## 4. Gates run on every change

| Check | Command | Pass |
|---|---|---|
| ERC | `kicad-cli sch erc fm1-midi-dongle.kicad_sch --severity-all` | 0 |
| Placement | end of `gen_pcb.py` | `placement issues: 0` |
| DRC | `kicad-cli pcb drc --severity-all --format json` | 0 unconnected. Only owner-known items remain (6 J1 edge pads, 0.8 mm text warnings). |
| Routing style | `check_routing.py <project>` | 0 any-angle, 0 90° corners, 0 acute angles (this board: 85.7% orthogonal, 14.3% 45°) |
| Loops | `python3 tools/check_loops.py` | 0 on every net |
| Schematic ↔ PCB parity | DRC parity section | No new items vs the last commit |
| Visual | renders, looked at by Claude | Nothing odd before reporting |

A regression in any gate is fixed before reporting, not reported as "mostly clean".

---

## 5. Gotchas learned on this board

- **SWIG iterator bug:** KiCad 10 SWIG with Python 3.14 breaks iteration in standalone scripts. Every script
  starts with:
  ```python
  if not hasattr(pcbnew.SwigPyIterator, 'next'):
      pcbnew.SwigPyIterator.next = pcbnew.SwigPyIterator.__next__
  ```
- **Deleting silk through SWIG corrupts the heap.** `silk.py` strips old silk from the `.kicad_pcb` text, then
  reloads the board.
- **Designators are footprint Reference fields, not board text.** Move the field.
- **EasyEDA courtyards = body outline.** They're useless for spacing; use pad bounding boxes plus F.Fab
  bodies.
- **Same-net pads may touch:** skip them in the spacing check, or you get false positives.
- **Zone fills go stale:** refill after routing. Run DRC on a fresh fill.
- **`gen_sch.py` writes `.kicad_pro`:** re-run `apply_rules.py` after it.
- **A new symbol must be written to both** the schematic's `lib_symbols` and the project `.kicad_sym`, or ERC
  warns "symbol not found".
- **Moving one part ripples:** U5 took TP3's spot, TP3 moved, its GND via then hit a B.Cu track. After any move,
  re-run the whole pipeline and every gate.
- **Datasheet pinout ≠ footprint pad order at rotation.** Write down the rotated pad map (e.g. SC-70-6 at 90°:
  top row 6-5-4, bottom row 1-2-3) before routing.

---

## 6. How each change was delivered

1. **Ask only when the choice is genuinely the owner's.** Give 2–4 options, with the recommended one first.
2. **Change the scripts** (sch → pcb → route → silk) and re-run the full pipeline.
3. **Run every gate in section 4.**
4. **Re-render everything:** 2D layers, the route and nets PNGs, 3D views.
5. **Update the records:** BOM.csv with a verification note, DESIGN.md with a dated section explaining why,
   and the cost estimate re-run at 50/100 boards.
6. **Report to the owner:** what changed and why, what moved, gate results, cost delta, open items, which
   images to look at. Then ask before committing.

---

## 7. Suggested skill structure

```
hw-codegen-board/
  SKILL.md              # sections 1, 3, 4, 6 condensed: pipeline, rules, gates, delivery
  references/
    gotchas.md          # section 5
    owner-rules.md      # section 3.1, the non-negotiables
  scripts/
    sch_gen_lib.py      # s-expr helpers, symbol copy, place(), custom-symbol writer (from gen_sch.py)
    pcb_gen_lib.py      # PLACE table loader, outline, planes, numeric checks (from gen_pcb.py)
    route_lib.py        # path()/via()/pour helpers + SWIG shim (from route.py)
    silk.py             # generic version of tools/silk.py, parameters in a dict
    check_loops.py      # already generic apart from the board path
    render_nets.py, render_route.py   # take the .kicad_pcb as an argument
    render_all.sh       # kicad-cli svg + rsvg-convert + 3D views
```

The project-specific parts are the net and pin maps, `PLACE`, the polylines, and `LABELS`/`INSIDE_OK`. Keep them
in the project's `tools/`. Move everything else into the skill.
